title: JSON contract monitor and alerting for structured model outputs
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build a lightweight, per-route JSON contract monitoring service that detects both syntactic and subtle semantic contract violations after model or config changes. The service will score incoming structured responses against a canonical contract (JSON contract) and baseline distributions, surface changes via the Console, and trigger alerts for significant regressions. Goal is to catch and quantify regressions introduced by model updates, prompt edits, or runtime config changes (e.g., sampling, temperature, truncation, quantization).
acceptance_criteria: A per-route contract definition can be uploaded to the Console or referenced from a stored eval set (Confluence link).
Incoming responses are validated for required keys, types, and value patterns; failures are recorded with a failure reason and example payload.
A delta score (contract drift score) is computed per hour and surfaced in a Console chart with historical baseline and confidence intervals.
Automatic email/Slack alerts fire when drift score exceeds threshold or error-rate jumps >5% relative to baseline for 3 consecutive windows.
An integration test verifies that a simulated model change that adds a missing key and one that changes a type both produce distinct failure reasons and increment metrics.
A lightweight opt-out flag is available per-customer/route to avoid noisy alerts during onboarding or experiments.
proposed_solution: Add a new service (contract-monitor) that subscribes to the request/response telemetry stream, applies a layered validator (syntactic rules -> type/pattern checks -> soft semantic assertions), aggregates statistics and produces a per-route drift score. Expose metrics via Prometheus and a Console endpoint. Provide a simple JSON contract DSL that can be authored in the Console or linked from an internal repo. Add a webhook/alerting integration and PR gating check that can mark a model deploy candidate as 'needs review' when contract-impacting regressions are detected.
tradeoffs_considered: Full strict schema enforcement at runtime vs. post-facto monitoring: chose post-facto monitoring to avoid customer-facing failures and allow graceful rollouts.

Heavyweight semantic evaluation (expensive embeddings/comparisons) vs. lightweight heuristics: implement a hybrid where heuristic checks run in real-time and semantic checks are batched for nightly re-evals.
Store full payloads for debugging vs. store only diffs/aggregates: store sampled full examples with TTL to ease debugging while keeping storage costs controlled.
implementation_steps: Define JSON contract DSL and Console authoring UI (product + design collaborate).
Instrument telemetry: ensure response bodies and routing metadata are available to the monitor service (privacy filters applied).
Build validator library in Rust for runtime speed; expose a thin Go/Python wrapper for the monitor service.
Implement drift scoring algorithm (baseline distribution + windowed KL-like divergence + error-rate factors).
Create Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards and Console charting components.
Add alerting rules and Slack/email webhook; add opt-out toggle for routes/customers.
E2E tests and chaos scenarios: simulate model/config changes in staging and validate alerts and dashboards.
Rollout via canary: enable for internal test accounts -> select customers -> global.
tests_and_eval: Unit tests for validator covering missing keys, type mismatches, pattern violations.
Integration test that runs a synthetic dataset through the monitor and asserts drift score semantics.
Nightly semantic re-eval job that computes example-level embedding similarity for flagged regressions (sampled).
Manual QA run with Design on Console UX for alert details and example drilldown.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal-only for platform and solutions accounts. Stage 2: opt-in beta for paying customers, enable webhooks. Stage 3: default-on for new routes with conservative thresholds and easy opt-out. Track false positive rate for two weeks before tightening thresholds.
